events.topic: GoTo EGM scheduled 14 October: treasury cancellation and board transition
events.title: GoTo EGM scheduled 14 October: treasury cancellation and board transition
events.summary: The official invitation schedules the meeting for 10:00–11:30 WIB on 14 October. It proposes retiring 32,186,417,803 Series A treasury shares and seeks approval for Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo’s resignation. The checked issuer page contains the invitation; an official resolution was not found.
events.implication: Reconcile issued shares, treasury shares and the weighted-average share denominator before changing per-share valuation. Cancellation is not a fresh buyback cash outflow.
events.how: Permanent cancellation may prevent reissuance of the identified treasury block. It does not mechanically improve EPS if the model already excludes those treasury shares. Board changes require the actual resolution and effective date.
events.nextAction: Check the official meeting summary, amendments and post-action register. Retain the current valuation denominator until verified.
events.evidence: Official invitation pp. 1–3 reviewed; not a meeting resolution

events.summary: Asian Banking & Finance interviews Superbank CFO Melisa Hendrawati about using behavioural data and AI in credit assessment, retaining human judgment and monitoring model bias and performance. The article does not quantify a default-rate improvement.
events.implication: Benchmark Bank Jago and GoPay lending on risk-adjusted returns, acquisition costs and model controls. AI adoption alone is not a verified underwriting advantage.
events.how: Broader behavioural signals may support thin-file borrower assessment. The commercial outcome depends on approval quality, losses, funding costs, privacy and operating execution.
events.nextAction: Compare vintage loss rates, approval conversion, cost per approved borrower and governance; seek quantified evidence before assigning a valuation premium.
events.evidence: Article and publisher listing reviewed; listing date 12 October, page relative timestamp varies

events.topic: ShopeePay Malaysia expands Zurich partnership into life insurance
events.title: ShopeePay Malaysia expands Zurich partnership into life insurance
events.summary: Zurich Life Insurance Malaysia announced distribution through ShopeePay and a two-year savings-and-protection plan starting at RM500. It builds on existing general-insurance partnerships; lower future entry premiums and family takaful are plans, not current launches.
events.implication: Use this Malaysian wallet cross-sell as a partnership benchmark for GoPay. Indonesia availability, licensing and economics are not established by the Malaysian launch.
events.how: Embedding insurance into wallet journeys may widen product breadth and retention. Conversion, fees, persistency and customer outcomes determine value.
events.nextAction: Screen licensed Indonesian insurer partnerships and customer demand, compare referral versus distribution structures and verify unit economics.
events.evidence: Official partner release reviewed; geographical scope retained

events.topic: Adjusted base-money growth slows to 9.3% in September
events.title: Adjusted base-money growth slows to 9.3% in September
events.summary: Bank Indonesia reports adjusted M0 of Rp2,353.1tn, growing 9.3% year on year versus 16.3% in August. The adjusted series accounts for liquidity-incentive effects; it is not M2.
events.implication: Adds a liquidity signal for bank funding and credit scenarios. Base money alone does not establish GoPay demand or Bank Jago deposit growth.
events.how: System liquidity can affect funding conditions alongside policy rates, deposit competition and currency pressure.
events.nextAction: Compare M2, deposit flows and lending rates; avoid equating a lower growth rate with an outright fall in the money stock.
events.evidence: Official release content reviewed; adjusted M0 definition retained

researchLibrary.title: ASEAN+3 Regional Economic Outlook 2026
researchLibrary.summaryBasis: Reviewed primary PDF — Foreword of actual PDF
researchLibrary.summary: AMRO highlights ASEAN+3 resilience, deeper regional demand links and the need for flexible policy amid trade and energy shocks.
takeaways: ASEAN+3 growth reached 4.3% in 2025.
AI investment and semiconductor exports helped offset trade disruption.
Energy import dependence creates material inflation and growth risks.
researchLibrary.implication: Evaluate regional expansion and partnership opportunities against country-specific demand and energy exposure, rather than applying one ASEAN growth assumption.
researchLibrary.evidenceScope: Selected executive/overview/country sections, not every page

researchLibrary.title: Asian Development Outlook, April 2026
researchLibrary.summaryBasis: Reviewed primary PDF — Foreword and Indonesia chapter Table 2.22.1 of actual PDF
researchLibrary.summary: ADB expects Indonesia to retain domestic-demand support while higher energy prices and geopolitical risk threaten regional resilience.
takeaways: Indonesia GDP growth is forecast at 5.2% in 2026 and 2027.
Indonesia inflation is forecast at 2.5% in both years.
The outlook assumes conflict does not become prolonged or substantially worse.
researchLibrary.implication: Connect consumption scenarios to orders and spending, and energy stress to driver economics; these April forecasts are not current realized data.
researchLibrary.evidenceScope: Selected executive/overview/country sections, not every page

researchLibrary.title: Asia-Pacific Private Equity Report 2026
researchLibrary.summaryBasis: Reviewed primary PDF — Overview and at-a-glance sections of actual PDF
researchLibrary.summary: Bain reports an uneven Asia-Pacific PE recovery: improving exits and distributions contrast with weak fundraising and elevated valuations.
takeaways: Net distributions turned positive after three years of outflows.
Fundraising reached a 12-year low; deal multiples rose to 13.4x.
AI disruption and operational value creation require deeper diligence.
researchLibrary.implication: Screen potential acquisitions for earnings quality, seller liquidity needs, and AI exposure; avoid assuming regional multiples justify a specific target price.
researchLibrary.evidenceScope: Selected executive/overview/country sections, not every page

researchLibrary.title: Global Private Equity Report 2026
researchLibrary.summaryBasis: Reviewed primary PDF — Actual PDF pages 3–8 overview
researchLibrary.summary: Bain describes a narrow global buyout recovery driven by megadeals, with liquidity and fundraising still constrained.
takeaways: 2025 buyout deal value rose 44% to US$904bn; exit value rose 47% to US$717bn.
Overall deal count declined 6%; 13 megadeals generated most value growth.
Distributions stayed below 15% of NAV for four years.
researchLibrary.implication: Prioritize proprietary sourcing and operational synergies; consider corporate buyers and liquidity-driven sellers, with careful scope comparisons.
researchLibrary.evidenceScope: Selected executive/overview/country sections, not every page

researchLibrary.title: Global Financial Stability Report, April 2026
researchLibrary.summaryBasis: Reviewed primary PDF — Executive summary of actual PDF
researchLibrary.summary: The IMF sees elevated financial-stability risk from conflict, tighter funding conditions and mechanisms that can amplify market shocks.
takeaways: Emerging markets face currency and capital-outflow pressures.
Nonbank investors transmit global risk shocks across borders.
Sovereign refinancing and leveraged financial positions can amplify stress.
researchLibrary.implication: Monitor rupiah exposure, market liquidity and funding availability alongside the business case for M&A and credit expansion.
researchLibrary.evidenceScope: Selected executive/overview/country sections, not every page

researchLibrary.title: World Economic Outlook, April 2026
researchLibrary.summaryBasis: Reviewed primary PDF — Executive summary of actual PDF
researchLibrary.summary: The IMF April reference forecast assumes limited Middle East conflict duration and warns that energy, inflation and financial-condition shocks could worsen the outlook.
takeaways: Reference global growth is 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027.
2026 global headline inflation is projected at 4.4%.
An adverse scenario reduces 2026 growth to 2.5%; the forecast is conditional.
researchLibrary.implication: Stress-test GoTo demand, driver fuel costs, credit losses and discount rates; retain report-date scenarios separately from realized outcomes.
researchLibrary.evidenceScope: Selected executive/overview/country sections, not every page

researchLibrary.title: Global Private Markets Report 2026
researchLibrary.summaryBasis: Reviewed primary PDF — Actual PDF pages 1–8 overview
researchLibrary.summary: McKinsey argues that operational value creation, disciplined entry pricing and liquidity management now matter more than cheap leverage and multiple expansion.
takeaways: Median PE purchase multiple increased to 11.8x EBITDA in 2025.
More than 16,000 PE-backed companies have been held for over four years.
About 70% of surveyed LPs planned to maintain or increase PE allocations.
researchLibrary.implication: Build each GoTo deal thesis around measurable operating improvements and integration milestones; include manager distributions and holding periods in fund monitoring.
researchLibrary.evidenceScope: Selected executive/overview/country sections, not every page

researchLibrary.title: Global Economic Prospects, June 2026
researchLibrary.summaryBasis: Reviewed primary PDF — Executive summary of actual PDF
researchLibrary.summary: The World Bank June outlook projects slower global activity amid energy disruptions, renewed inflation and constrained policy space.
takeaways: Global growth is forecast at 2.5% in 2026, down from 2.9% in 2025.
Emerging-market and developing-economy growth is forecast at 3.6%.
Debt and energy-price shocks can worsen financing conditions.
researchLibrary.implication: Use a downside consumption and funding scenario in valuation; compare differences in dates and methodology before treating IMF and World Bank projections as disagreement.
researchLibrary.evidenceScope: Selected executive/overview/country sections, not every page

researchLibrary.title: WEO October 2026 Chapter 3: corporate tax and cross-border spillovers
researchLibrary.summary: The IMF finds that tax differences affect investment location and profit allocation, while anti-avoidance rules increasingly align profits with real activity. The effects of tax cuts depend on how governments finance them.
researchLibrary.relevance: Analyst application: assess tax substance, transfer pricing, intellectual-property ownership and after-tax cash flows when structuring cross-border investments. This chapter does not establish a change to Indonesian law.
takeaways: Headline statutory rates do not capture the full effective tax burden.
Investment location, profit allocation and financing have different tax and economic channels.
Model after-tax returns and obtain jurisdiction-specific tax advice before preferring a holding structure.
researchLibrary.evidence: October issue; publication day not established for this chapter. PDF opening analysis pp. 1–3 and tax-mechanism discussion p. 5 reviewed; not a full WEO forecast review.

researchLibrary.title: September 2026 adjusted base money: growth and liquidity-incentive basis
researchLibrary.summary: Bank Indonesia reports adjusted M0 of Rp2,353.1tn, growing 9.3% year on year versus 16.3% in August. The adjusted series accounts for liquidity-incentive effects; it is not M2.

Assess liquidity together with bank funding and credit data.

policyWatch.title: BNPL licensing and customer protection
policyWatch.fact: POJK 32/2025 permits BNPL through commercial banks and financing companies. Financing companies require prior OJK approval. Disclosure, data protection, collections and reporting are covered.
policyWatch.implication: Validate the actual lending entity, authorization and partner responsibilities when screening a BNPL investment or distribution agreement.
policyWatch.nextAction: Map product → licensed lender → approval and consumer-disclosure obligations.
policyWatch.evidence: Official regulatory announcement reviewed; legal application depends on the lending entity.

policyWatch.title: BNPL borrower checks apply from 1 July 2026
policyWatch.fact: PADK 2/2026 requires age 18 or married status and average gross income of at least Rp3m per month, supported by valid evidence. Borrower checks apply to new acquisitions and extensions no later than 1 July 2026.
policyWatch.implication: Income verification already affects eligible customer acquisition. The repayment-to-income ceiling is 40% in 2027–28 and 30% from 2029; test affordability and origination economics at the financing-company lender.
policyWatch.nextAction: Audit current onboarding evidence and model future affordability limits. The older January 2027 announcement is historical; the newer rule sets July 2026 for borrower checks.
policyWatch.evidence: OJK regulatory page and official FAQ questions 6–8 reviewed; PADK adopted 4 May 2026. Financing-company scope differs from bank BNPL.

policyWatch.title: Payment-industry reform: capability and risk requirements
policyWatch.scope: Payment providers, infrastructure and supporting companies
policyWatch.fact: PBI 10/2025 and PADG 32/2025 introduce the payment-industry framework, including TIKMI: transactions, interconnection, competency, risk management and IT infrastructure.
policyWatch.implication: Payments acquisitions and partnerships need a capability and integration assessment alongside revenue synergies; cyber resilience and infrastructure can require investment.
policyWatch.nextAction: Assess the target’s authorization, connectivity, risk controls and technology against the relevant category.
policyWatch.evidence: Official policy announcement and implementation-guide introduction reviewed.

policyWatch.title: QRIS merchant mix changes payment unit economics
policyWatch.scope: Micro and regular merchants; merchant discount rate
policyWatch.fact: The current BI table lists 0% MDR for micro-merchant transactions up to Rp500,000, 0.3% above that amount, and 0.7% for small, medium and large regular merchants. MDR is an industry fee, not wholly GoTo revenue.
policyWatch.implication: Merchant count and transaction growth do not translate directly into payment revenue. Merchant category, ticket size, fee sharing and service costs determine contribution.
policyWatch.nextAction: Segment merchant volumes and net fee realization; avoid applying the 0.7% rate to every QRIS transaction.
policyWatch.evidence: Official tariff table reviewed; page publication date not established. The same zero-rate threshold also appears in BI’s 2024 annual report.

policyWatch.title: M&A notification: control, Indonesia nexus and timing
policyWatch.scope: Share / asset acquisitions and mergers meeting the criteria
policyWatch.fact: PerKPPU 3/2023 requires qualifying transactions to be notified within 30 working days after legal effectiveness. It considers thresholds, control changes, affiliation and Indonesian assets or sales. A minority stake can confer control.
policyWatch.implication: Include notification analysis and the legal-effective date in the deal timetable; minority structure alone does not resolve competition review.
policyWatch.nextAction: Have counsel assess the criteria using group structure and Indonesian assets / sales before signing.
policyWatch.evidence: Regulation Articles 1–3 and 6–10 reviewed; transaction-specific legal assessment remains required.

signals.title: GoTo EGM scheduled 14 October: treasury cancellation and board transition
signals.summary: The official invitation schedules the meeting for 10:00–11:30 WIB on 14 October. It proposes retiring 32,186,417,803 Series A treasury shares and seeks approval for Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo’s resignation. The checked issuer page contains the invitation; an official resolution was not found.
signals.implication: Reconcile issued shares, treasury shares and the weighted-average share denominator before changing per-share valuation. Cancellation is not a fresh buyback cash outflow.
signals.how: Permanent cancellation may prevent reissuance of the identified treasury block. It does not mechanically improve EPS if the model already excludes those treasury shares. Board changes require the actual resolution and effective date.
signals.nextAction: Check the official meeting summary, amendments and post-action register. Retain the current valuation denominator until verified.
signals.evidence: Official invitation pp. 1–3 reviewed; not a meeting resolution

signals.title: VinFast offers dealers up to US$60,000 per electric-motorcycle showroom
signals.summary: TNGlobal reports a dealer package in Indonesia and the Philippines: up to US$40,000 base support, up to US$5,000 for opening by 31 October and up to US$15,000 for partners opening at least three stores. Eligibility and showroom standards apply.
signals.implication: Distribution incentives could affect Electrum’s dealer access and driver-EV options. Compare vehicle financing, swap coverage and operating cost before estimating a competitive effect.
signals.how: Dealer subsidies lower channel-entry cost; announced incentives do not prove deployed showrooms, fleet adoption or lost GoTo share.
signals.nextAction: Verify eligible Indonesian locations, dealer openings, battery-swap coverage and driver total cost of ownership.
signals.status: Reported dealer program; rollout to verify
signals.evidence: Full TNGlobal article reviewed; issuer statement described by publisher

signals.title: Superbank describes AI-assisted assessment of underserved borrowers
signals.summary: Asian Banking & Finance interviews Superbank CFO Melisa Hendrawati about using behavioural data and AI in credit assessment, retaining human judgment and monitoring model bias and performance. The article does not quantify a default-rate improvement.
signals.implication: Benchmark Bank Jago and GoPay lending on risk-adjusted returns, acquisition costs and model controls. AI adoption alone is not a verified underwriting advantage.
signals.how: Broader behavioural signals may support thin-file borrower assessment. The commercial outcome depends on approval quality, losses, funding costs, privacy and operating execution.
signals.nextAction: Compare vintage loss rates, approval conversion, cost per approved borrower and governance; seek quantified evidence before assigning a valuation premium.
signals.evidence: Article and publisher listing reviewed; listing date 12 October, page relative timestamp varies

signals.title: ShopeePay Malaysia expands Zurich partnership into life insurance
signals.summary: Zurich Life Insurance Malaysia announced distribution through ShopeePay and a two-year savings-and-protection plan starting at RM500. It builds on existing general-insurance partnerships; lower future entry premiums and family takaful are plans, not current launches.
signals.implication: Use this Malaysian wallet cross-sell as a partnership benchmark for GoPay. Indonesia availability, licensing and economics are not established by the Malaysian launch.
signals.how: Embedding insurance into wallet journeys may widen product breadth and retention. Conversion, fees, persistency and customer outcomes determine value.
signals.nextAction: Screen licensed Indonesian insurer partnerships and customer demand, compare referral versus distribution structures and verify unit economics.
signals.evidence: Official partner release reviewed; geographical scope retained

signals.title: Adjusted base-money growth slows to 9.3% in September
signals.summary: Bank Indonesia reports adjusted M0 of Rp2,353.1tn, growing 9.3% year on year versus 16.3% in August. The adjusted series accounts for liquidity-incentive effects; it is not M2.
signals.implication: Adds a liquidity signal for bank funding and credit scenarios. Base money alone does not establish GoPay demand or Bank Jago deposit growth.
signals.how: System liquidity can affect funding conditions alongside policy rates, deposit competition and currency pressure.
signals.nextAction: Compare M2, deposit flows and lending rates; avoid equating a lower growth rate with an outright fall in the money stock.
signals.evidence: Official release content reviewed; adjusted M0 definition retained

research.title: WEO October 2026 Chapter 3: corporate tax and cross-border spillovers
research.summary: The IMF finds that tax differences affect investment location and profit allocation, while anti-avoidance rules increasingly align profits with real activity. The effects of tax cuts depend on how governments finance them.
research.relevance: Analyst application: assess tax substance, transfer pricing, intellectual-property ownership and after-tax cash flows when structuring cross-border investments. This chapter does not establish a change to Indonesian law.
takeaways: Headline statutory rates do not capture the full effective tax burden.
Investment location, profit allocation and financing have different tax and economic channels.
Model after-tax returns and obtain jurisdiction-specific tax advice before preferring a holding structure.
research.evidence: October issue; publication day not established for this chapter. PDF opening analysis pp. 1–3 and tax-mechanism discussion p. 5 reviewed; not a full WEO forecast review.
